summary: Independently verified the production deploy of FINTRACK-25 (Alert Justification Feedback Loop). First verification attempt (deployment c34211ce, commit f3d64ce) found a real gap: /openapi.json did not show the new POST /api/v1/alerts/{alert_id}/justify route despite Railway reporting SUCCESS and clean deploy logs. Investigated: build log showed an unusually fast (<1s active work), heavily-cached build. Set NO_CACHE=1 on the service (Monty's explicit go-ahead) and triggered a clean rebuild (deployment 3f227209, same commit f3d64ce, ~44s build vs ~2s cached) -- re-check still showed the route missing on a plain GET. A cache-busted GET (?cb=...) on the SAME deployment immediately returned the correct schema with /justify present, pointing to an HTTP-level cached response (not necessarily Railway's Docker build cache) as the more likely actual cause -- root cause is not fully certain, flagged honestly rather than overclaiming. Removed NO_CACHE from the service afterward (via Railway's own agent, staged for the next deploy only, no redeploy triggered) so future merges keep using fast cached builds, per Monty's explicit concern about paying this cost on every merge. Final verification (cache-busted): /health -> ok, /health/ready -> ready, /openapi.json confirms POST /api/v1/alerts/{alert_id}/justify live with correct path, method, auth requirement, and 204/422 response shapes matching the code. Deploy logs confirm alembic migration 0009 ran clean (new alert_justifications table, no changes to existing tables) and Uvicorn started without error. No CI/CD workflow changes required -- additive-only migration, no new secrets, no frontend changes. Rollback: git revert HEAD && git push origin main, back to 90ad9ddb371ad75ddd6ef37080122402aa4dd773 (last known-good commit before this story's docs-only follow-up). Follow-up proposed (not built in this pass): fold a cache-busted schema/route check into the pending Railway healthcheck task (F-team backlog item) so staleness -- build-cache or HTTP-cache -- is caught automatically post-deploy rather than via manual Release Pro spot-check.
